policy_title: Build 10,000 new detention places and expand prison capacity
stated: Reform UK will start building 10,000 new state-built and managed detention places and expand prison capacity, commissioning disused military bases if needed, to ensure 'life means life' for those who endanger the public.

source.quote: Start Building of 10,000 New Detention Places Start expansion in capacity of state built and managed prisons so that life means life for those who endanger the public. Commission disused military bases if needed.

bearing_set.reason: Expanding detention capacity and mandating 'life means life' sentences directly affects justice-system capacity, sentencing policy, and the state's ability to keep dangerous offenders off the streets — core O5 indicators.

Building 10,000 new state-managed detention places represents a large capital commitment (plausibly £2–3bn at typical UK prison construction costs) plus hundreds of millions annually in running costs; this is a concrete, material fiscal impact that would affect the funded/borrowed balance of public spending.

membership_note: The policy bears primarily on the protective justice outcome (O5) and on public finances (O12) due to the scale of the capital and operational spending implied. O10 (personal liberty) does not apply at the non-negligible bar here — the coercive power is applied to convicted/detained individuals within existing criminal justice scope, not to free citizens via surveillance, speech limits or mandates. O14 (inequality) via differential incarceration rates is a plausible second-order effect but too indirect to clear the bar without a specific mechanism tied to this policy's design.
